subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 48-year-old man presents with a 1-day history of excruciating pain, redness, and swelling of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. He has hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide and has had similar episodes in the past. Synovial fluid analysis shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. He is not currently taking any urate-lowering medication.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate management at this time?

options.text: Begin allopurinol at a high dose and continue it during the acute attack
Treat with colchicine or an NSAID and defer urate-lowering therapy until the attack resolves
Start probenecid to increase urinary uric acid excretion
Start pegloticase for rapid urate lowering

explanation_correct: An acute gout attack is treated with anti-inflammatory therapy, classically colchicine, an NSAID, or corticosteroids. Colchicine binds tubulin and inhibits neutrophil activation and migration, while NSAIDs reduce the inflammatory response to monosodium urate crystals. Urate-lowering drugs such as allopurinol are not initiated during an acute attack because rapid shifts in uric acid can prolong or precipitate an attack; they are started after the flare resolves, often with anti-inflammatory prophylaxis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Starting allopurinol during an acute flare can worsen or prolong the attack and is not the initial management.
explanation_incorrect.C: Probenecid is a uricosuric agent used for chronic urate lowering and has no role in treating the acute inflammation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Low-dose aspirin raises uric acid by reducing renal excretion and is not an appropriate analgesic for acute gout.
explanation_incorrect.E: Pegloticase is a PEGylated uricase reserved for severe, refractory chronic tophaceous gout and is not used for an acute uncomplicated attack.

educationalObjective: Acute gout is treated with colchicine, an NSAID, or corticosteroids, while urate-lowering therapy such as allopurinol is deferred until the flare resolves.
